title: Why Use Tera from DuckDB?
description: Render [Tera](https://keats.github.io/tera/) templates inside SQL with JSON context. Tera is a [Jinja2-inspired](https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/) template engine written in Rust; this extension makes it a scalar function so each query row can produce its own rendered string — emails, config blocks, dynamic SQL, Slack payloads, IaC fragments — without leaving DuckDB.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Anywhere you'd otherwise pull rows out of DuckDB just to feed them into a template loop in Python or Node, [`tera_render`](#tera_render) collapses that loop into a single SQL projection. The template stays declarative; the data stays in the query.

bulletPoints.label: Per-row HTML / email
bulletPoints.description: Build the body of a transactional email per row: pass the row's columns as a JSON object via [`json_object`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/json) and render against a template literal.

bulletPoints.label: Config-file generation
bulletPoints.description: Materialize one nginx / systemd / Kubernetes manifest per row of a configuration table. Disable autoescape with `autoescape := false` for non-HTML output.

bulletPoints.label: Dynamic SQL
bulletPoints.description: Use Tera as a meta-SQL preprocessor — render `SELECT ... FROM {{ table }} WHERE {{ pred }}` against context columns, then execute the result. Treat templates as trusted; Tera interpolation is not parameter-safe.

bulletPoints.label: Notifications and webhook payloads
bulletPoints.description: Render Slack / PagerDuty / webhook JSON bodies from query results so a single SQL pipeline takes you from event to delivered message.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: A scalar function backed by the [Tera](https://github.com/Keats/tera) Rust crate. Each call compiles (or reuses a cached) template, binds the JSON context, and returns the rendered text. There is no `ATTACH`, no secrets — the function surface is one name and a few optional named arguments.

bulletPoints.label: Inline and file-backed templates
bulletPoints.description: The first argument is either an inline template string or a template name. Pass `template_path := './templates/*.html'` to load templates from disk by name; this enables `{% extends %}` / `{% include %}` across the matched files. See Tera's [inheritance docs](https://keats.github.io/tera/docs/#inheritance).

bulletPoints.label: JSON context
bulletPoints.description: The second argument is a `JSON` value — a literal string, [`json_object(...)`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/json), or a column. Nested objects, arrays, and primitives are all addressable as `{{ user.name }}`, `{% for x in items %}`, `{{ items | length }}`.

bulletPoints.label: Autoescape on by default
bulletPoints.description: HTML special characters in context values are escaped — safe default for HTML / email output. Pass `autoescape := false` when generating raw text (configs, SQL, JSON payloads).

bulletPoints.label: Full Tera vocabulary
bulletPoints.description: Filters (`upper`, `lower`, `length`, `default`, `join`, `date`, `truncate`, etc.), control flow (`if` / `elif` / `else`, `for` with `loop.index` / `loop.last`), inheritance, macros, and includes — see the [Tera manual](https://keats.github.io/tera/docs/) for the full surface.

sections.title: Tera vs MiniJinja
sections.description: This catalog ships two Jinja-style template engines as DuckDB extensions: [Tera](#) and [`minijinja`](/products/extensions/minijinja). They overlap heavily — both render `{{ var }}` / `{% for %}` / `{% if %}` against JSON context. The differences are real but small.

bulletPoints.label: Pick Tera for the bigger feature surface
bulletPoints.description: Tera ships a wider [built-in filter and tester library](https://keats.github.io/tera/docs/#built-ins), template inheritance via `template_path`, and macros — choose Tera when your templates lean on Jinja2's richer authoring features.

bulletPoints.label: Pick MiniJinja for speed and Jinja2 fidelity
bulletPoints.description: [MiniJinja](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/minijinja) targets strict Python-Jinja2 semantics with a tiny, fast core. Choose [`minijinja`](/products/extensions/minijinja) when you want behavior that matches an existing Python Jinja codebase, or when render-rate per row matters most.

bulletPoints.label: Either is fine for everyday substitution
bulletPoints.description: For `{{ name }}` / `{{ x | upper }}` / `{% for x in xs %}`, both produce identical output. Lock in whichever syntax matches your team's existing templates.

useCases.title: Render transactional emails per row
useCases.description: One row per recipient, one [`tera_render`](#tera_render) call producing the HTML body — fed straight into a downstream sender.

useCases.title: Generate per-host configuration
useCases.description: A `virtual_hosts` table plus a single Tera template equals one rendered nginx / Caddy / Envoy block per host, ready to write to disk or push to a config repo.

useCases.title: Build dynamic SQL from metadata
useCases.description: Drive `SELECT` / `CREATE TABLE` shape from a metadata table — Tera renders the SQL, your driver executes it. Useful for codegen, schema migrations, and templated reporting.

useCases.title: Format Slack / webhook payloads
useCases.description: Render alert JSON bodies directly from the query that detected the alert. Pair with [`http_client`](/products/extensions/http_client) to deliver them in the same pipeline.
